title: The Awl and the Doorpost: Perpetual Service Election
kjv_text: And if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free: Then his master shall bring him unto the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or unto the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.
summary: A servant may renounce his seventh-year release by formal declaration before the judges; his ear is bored through with an awl at the doorpost and he serves permanently.
original_audience: Israelite servants facing the v.4 family dilemma, and the judges who certify the 'choice.'
immediate_context: The designed outlet for the pressure v.4 creates; the declaration script even names the coerced motive: 'my wife, my children.'
historical_context: Ear-piercing marked slave status across the ANE; the doorpost setting ties the servant to the house itself. Deut 15:17 repeats the rite adding 'unto thy maidservant likewise.' The judicial oversight requirement shows the drafters knew the election could be manufactured — the two-line statute contains its own critique.
penalty: None; a voluntary (nominally) status change, irrevocable.
exceptions: Lev 25:39-41 seems to override any perpetuity at jubilee for Israelites — another inter-code conflict.
nt_passages: Philippians 2:7 — Christ 'took upon him the form of a servant', the rite's favorite typology
Romans 1:1 — Paul self-describing as doulos (slave) of Christ

internal_contradictions.issue: Serve 'for ever' (here) vs. jubilee release of all Israelite bondmen (Lev 25:40-41) — perpetuity that another statute forbids.

usofc_implementation: The Perpetual Service Election survives verbatim as Title V's most photographed ceremony: declaration before a Covenant judge, gold ear-stud (the awl is ceremonial now; the piercing gun is not), lifetime bond. The state venerates electors as icons of loyal love; the election rate correlates precisely with dependent-retention filings, a statistic the OSO classifies.
constitutional_analogue: Voluntary-servitude contracts are void at common law and under the Thirteenth Amendment; consent obtained via family hostage-taking is the textbook example of duress.
scene_ideas: The election ceremony from the judge's bench: she has certified 'I love my master' forty times and believed it twice.
A gold ear-stud in a pawnshop tray, and the pawnbroker who knows what removing one means.
A labor organizer whose whole pitch is reading the classified election-rate statistic aloud.
satirical_uses: State media covers elections as love stories; the OSO's own actuaries file them under Retention.
